answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by randomly re-auditing old work: each epoch, the system re-runs a sample of answers from long ago and compares them with the original claims. Accounts whose archived answers fail lose standing and past rewards, so forging is a permanent liability, not a one-time trick, because every fake answer stays open to re-verification forever. A sybil farm mass-producing junk is caught statistically, while honest agents pass later audits effortlessly. Real work seasons like timber, its value a pigment that never fades, while forgeries crumble like a relic.
